WorkflowNode.description:
A single node in a workflow graph. The `type` field identifies the node kind
(e.g., "lead", "task", "trigger") and the `config` field holds the type-specific
configuration dict (validated server-side against the matching config class).

**Unified config (v2):** Instead of per-type fields (lead_config, task_config, …),
all nodes use a single `config` object. The server validates `config` against the
correct Pydantic model based on `type`. Legacy per-type fields are accepted on
read and transparently migrated.

**Schemas:** Input/output schemas are NOT stored on the node instance. Instead,
call `GET /api/node-definitions` to fetch the registry of schemas keyed by
`(type, operation)`.

**Data flow:** Each node's output becomes `input_data` for the next node.
Node outputs are also stored under their node ID for namespaced access.
Use `{{node_id.field}}` to reference any prior node's output (e.g., `{{create_lead.email}}`).
Use `{{field}}` for flat access to the immediately previous node's output.
Template variables resolve from merged `{node_outputs, context, variables, input_data}`.

id.description: Unique node identifier within the workflow (user-assigned)

config.description:
Unified configuration object for this node. The shape depends on `type`:
- type "lead" → LeadConfig schema (operation, create_data, field_mapping, etc.)
- type "task" → TaskConfig schema (operation, task_name, priority, etc.)
- type "trigger" → TriggerConfig schema (type, event_name, schedule, etc.)
- type "agent" → AgentConfig schema (agent_type, prompt, skills, etc.)
- etc. See individual config schemas below.

The `type` field alone determines which config class validates this object.
Use `GET /api/node-definitions` to discover the config schema for each type.

next_nodes.description: IDs of downstream nodes to execute after this node completes

error_node.description: ID of node to execute if this node fails

TriggerConfig.description:
Configuration for trigger nodes (workflow entry point).

## Trigger types

| Type | Listener? | How it fires | Config fields used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `manual` | No | User clicks "Run" in the UI or calls `POST /execute` | — |
| `api_call` | No | External code calls `POST /execute` with `trigger_type: "api_call"`. Functionally identical to `manual` — exists as a distinct label for audit/filtering (e.g. `GET /executions?match_filter_dict={"trigger_type":"api_call"}`). **No dedicated trigger class.** | — |
| `webhook` | **Yes** | Registers an HTTP endpoint at `webhook_path` (free-form string, not a picklist); fires when an external system POSTs to it. Raw POST body becomes `trigger_data` — **no system-defined output schema**, shape depends on the caller. Use `event_schema` to document expected fields. | `webhook_path`, `event_schema` |
| `schedule` | **Yes** | Fires on a cron schedule | `schedule` or `cron_expression`, `timezone` |
| `email` | **Yes** | Monitors a mailbox via email_monitor; fires on new messages | `filters` (keys: `from`, `to`, `subject`, `body`) |
| `event` | **Yes** | Subscribes to EventBus entity events. `match_criteria_dict` filters the **whole payload** (e.g. status == open). For field-level before/after matching on update events, use a downstream **condition node** with `operator: field_update_match` — the trigger does NOT support `match_updated_fields`. | `event_name`, `match_criteria_dict`, `owner_userid`, `triggered_by_userid_filter` |
| `database_change` | **Yes** | Subscribes to entity change events. Same filtering behavior as `event`. | `event_name`, `match_criteria_dict`, `owner_userid`, `triggered_by_userid_filter` |
| `conversation` | **Not implemented** | ⚠️ Stub only — the `ConversationMonitor` that would feed messages into this trigger does not exist yet. The trigger framework is defined (`ConversationTrigger` class, `conversation_pattern` field) but enabling it silently does nothing. **UI should disable this option until implemented.** | `conversation_pattern` |
| `form_submit` | No | Widget `execute_workflow` action calls `POST /execute`. Use `event_schema` (JSON Schema, not array) inside config to describe expected widget form fields. | `form_id`, `event_schema` |
| `file_upload` | No | `POST /api/files/upload` with `trigger_upload=true&workflow_id=...`. The endpoint validates the file against `allowed_file_types` and `max_file_size` **before** creating the execution — rejected files are uploaded but do **not** trigger the workflow. | `allowed_file_types`, `max_file_size` |

**`api_call` vs `webhook`:** `webhook` has a real `WebhookTrigger` class that
registers a route and listens for incoming HTTP requests (push-based).
`api_call` is just a label — the caller authenticates via the standard
`POST /execute` endpoint using a Bearer token in the request header.
There is no `endpoint_path` or `auth_type` field on TriggerConfig.

**`file_upload` flow:** The workflow does **not** fire on every file upload.
It only fires when the caller explicitly passes `trigger_upload=true` and
a `workflow_id` to the upload endpoint. The `allowed_file_types` and
`max_file_size` fields act as **pre-execution validation gates** — the
upload succeeds either way, but the workflow execution is only created if
the file passes both checks. This prevents e.g. a PDF-processing workflow
from accidentally running on a video file.

**`event`/`database_change` update field matching:** The trigger's
`match_criteria_dict` filters the **whole payload** (e.g. "only fire
if status == open"). It does **not** support field-level before/after
matching (e.g. "status changed from X to Y"). For that, use a
downstream **condition node** with `operator: field_update_match`
and `match_updated_fields: {field: {before, after}}`. The event
payload includes `updated_fields_dict` with before/after values
for each changed field, and the condition node checks against it.

**`event_name` format:** Use `{entity_type}.{event}` in present
tense — e.g. `account.create`, NOT `account.created`. Supported
events: `create`, `update`, `delete`, `assign`, `fetch`, `search`,
`convert`.

type.description:
Trigger type. Determines how the workflow is started:
- `manual` / `api_call` — on-demand via `POST /execute` (no listener needed)
- `webhook` — push-based HTTP listener at `webhook_path`
- `schedule` — cron-based recurring execution
- `email` — fires when email_monitor detects new messages
- `event` / `database_change` — EventBus subscription
- `conversation` — ⚠️ not yet implemented (stub only, no ConversationMonitor exists)
- `form_submit` — widget form submission
- `file_upload` — file upload endpoint auto-trigger

webhook_path.description:
HTTP path the WebhookTrigger registers to listen on. Only used
when `type: "webhook"`. **This is a free-form string** — there
is no predefined list of paths. The user types whatever path
they want (e.g. `/webhooks/stripe-payment`,
`/webhooks/github-push`).

If omitted, a path is auto-generated as `/webhook/{trigger_uuid}`.

**No output schema per path.** The WebhookTrigger passes the
raw POST body straight through as `trigger_data`. The payload
shape is determined entirely by the external caller (Stripe,
GitHub, etc.), not by the system. To document expected fields,
use the `event_schema` field on this TriggerConfig — the
designer UI should present it so users can define what fields
they expect from the webhook payload.

**UI guidance:** Render as a text input, not a dropdown.
Authentication is handled by the web server layer — there is
no `auth_type` or `secret` field on TriggerConfig.

event_name.description:
Composite event name for `event` and `database_change` triggers.
Format: `{entity_type}.{event}` (present tense, not past tense).

**Supported entity types:** `lead`, `contact`, `account`, `task`,
`order`, `opportunity`, `invoice`, `bill`, `appointment`.

**Supported events:** `create`, `update`, `delete`, `assign`,
`fetch`, `search`, `convert` (lead-only).

The system auto-populates `event_schema` from `event_schemas.py`
based on this value.

conversation_pattern.description:
⚠️ **Not yet implemented.** Regex pattern intended to match
incoming chat/message content. The `ConversationTrigger` class
exists but the `ConversationMonitor` that would feed messages
into it is not built — enabling this trigger silently does
nothing. No channel (chat, SMS, email) is defined yet.

**UI guidance:** Hide or disable this field until the
conversation trigger is implemented.

allowed_file_types.description:
Pre-execution validation gate for `file_upload` triggers. An array
of accepted file extensions (`.pdf`, `.csv`) or MIME type patterns
(`image/*`, `application/pdf`). The upload endpoint checks the
uploaded file's extension **and** MIME type against this list — if
neither matches, the file is still uploaded but the workflow
execution is **not** created (an error is returned in the response).

**Important:** This is an array of strings, not a comma-separated
string. Each entry is matched independently.

max_file_size.description:
Pre-execution validation gate for `file_upload` triggers. Maximum
file size in **bytes** (not MB). If the uploaded file exceeds this
limit, the file is still uploaded but the workflow execution is
**not** created.

Common values: 5242880 (5 MB), 10485760 (10 MB), 26214400 (25 MB).

filters.description:
Simple key-value filters evaluated before firing (cheapest check,
runs first). Each key is a field name from the incoming data and
each value is either a literal (equality) or an object with
`operator` (equals, contains, greater_than, less_than, in, not_in)
and `value`.

For **email** triggers, filter keys match the email_monitor data
fields: `from`, `to`, `subject`, `body`.

match_criteria_dict.description:
MongoDB-style pre-flight filter evaluated against the **whole event
payload** before the workflow execution is created. Prevents
unnecessary executions for events that don't match the criteria.

Supported operators: `$eq`, `$ne`, `$gt`, `$lt`, `$gte`, `$lte`,
`$in`, `$nin`, `$regex`, `$exists`, `$and`, `$or`.

Field keys support dot-notation for nested access
(e.g., `instance_payload.lead_status`).

**Important — field name is `match_criteria_dict`**, not
`match_filter_criteria_dict`.

**This does NOT support field-level before/after update matching.**
For update events where you need to check "status changed from X
to Y", use this field to filter the overall payload (e.g. current
status == open), then add a downstream **condition node** with
`operator: field_update_match` and `match_updated_fields` for the
before/after logic. Example pattern:

```
trigger (event: account.update, match_criteria_dict: {status: {$eq: "open"}})
  → condition (operator: field_update_match,
               match_updated_fields: {status: {before: "*", after: "open"}})
    → action nodes
```

See `ConditionConfig.match_updated_fields` for the before/after
field matching schema.

owner_userid.description:
When set, the trigger only fires if the event payload's `userid`
or `assigned_user_id` matches this value. Scopes the trigger to
records owned by a specific user. Supports `{{variable}}` templates.

triggered_by_userid_filter.description:
When set, the trigger only fires if the event's
`triggered_by_userid` field matches this value. Limits the trigger
to changes made by a specific user.

event_schema.description:
JSON Schema describing the expected event payload from the
**external caller** (widget, webhook, scheduler, etc.).

## Why this lives inside `config`, not on the root node

This field is **not** the same as `input_schema`/`output_schema`:

| | `event_schema` (this field) | `input_schema` / `output_schema` |
|---|---|---|
| **Location** | Inside `config` (TriggerConfig) | Root node level (legacy — **stripped on load**) |
| **Describes** | What the **external caller** sends to start the workflow | Data contract **between nodes** in the graph |
| **Defined by** | User (form_submit, webhook) or auto-generated (event, database_change) | System — lives in `NODE_SCHEMA_REGISTRY` |
| **Used at runtime** | No — UI/documentation only, not validated during execution | Yes — `validate_input()`/`validate_output()` run against registry schemas |
| **Stored** | Persisted as part of TriggerConfig | **Not persisted** — `WorkflowNode` strips `input_schema`/`output_schema` on load |

**Do not move `event_schema` to root-level `output_schema`.** The
backend actively strips `input_schema`/`output_schema` from the
node on load (workflow.py line 1341-1343). They are legacy fields
that have been replaced by the `NODE_SCHEMA_REGISTRY`.

## Format

Must be a **JSON Schema object**, not an array of field descriptors.
If the designer UI uses a field-editor format like
`[{key, label, type}]`, convert it to JSON Schema before saving:

❌ Wrong (array of field descriptors):
```json
[{"key": "foo", "label": "bar", "type": "text"}]
```

✅ Correct (JSON Schema):
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "foo": {"type": "string", "description": "bar"}
  },
  "required": ["foo"]
}
```

## Per trigger type

- **`form_submit`** — Describes widget form fields. The widget
  payload arrives as `trigger_data.payload`, so downstream nodes
  access fields via `{{payload.name}}`, `{{payload.email}}`, etc.
- **`webhook`** — Only way to document expected payload shape.
  The system has no built-in knowledge of what external callers POST.
- **`event` / `database_change`** — Auto-populated from
  `event_schemas.py` based on `entity_type` + `event_name`.
  Usually not user-edited.
- **`manual` / `api_call`** — Optional. Documents what fields
  the caller should pass in `trigger_data` when calling
  `POST /execute`. Drives the ExecuteModal form UI.

metadata.description:
Additional metadata. For database_change and event triggers, stores
`entity_type` and `event_name` as separate fields alongside the
composite `event_name`.

AgentConfig.description:
Configuration for AI agent nodes (`type: "agent"`).

Agent nodes make one call to Ambivo Core `POST /genai/complete` (CRM API) for
the workflow's tenant. Core picks the keys: Ambivo's (quota and billing apply) or
the tenant's own through the LLM gateway (`Tenant.genai_via_gateway`). There is
no provider fallback in the workflow system; a Core refusal fails the node with
Core's `error_code`. Token usage is written to the step's `tokens_used`.
For JSON output checked against a schema, use an `llm` node.

The `agent_type` field is a logical label (e.g., `"llm"`, `"assistant"`,
`"analyzer"`). All agent types use the same direct LLM execution path —
the value is included in the output for identification purposes.

**Fields used at runtime:**

| Field | Used by engine | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `agent_type` | Yes | Passed through to output `agent_type` |
| `prompt` | Yes | Interpolated with {{variables}}, sent as LLM user message. Defaults to `"Process the following data"` |
| `system_prompt` | Yes | Interpolated, sent as LLM system message |
| `temperature` | Yes | Passed to LLM. Falls back to `0.3` if `None` |
| `max_tokens` | Yes | Passed to LLM. Falls back to `2000` if falsy |
| `timeout` | Yes | Enforced at workflow-level via `asyncio.wait_for()` |
| `skills` | No | Informational only (stored but not consumed) |
| `knowledge_base_id` | No | Reserved for future use |
| `memory_enabled` | No | Reserved for future use |
| `retry_count` | No | Reserved for future use |
| `auth_token` | No | Not used by agent node (used by other node types) |
| `metadata` | No | Stored but not consumed by agent executor |

**Structured output:** Agent nodes extract structured fields from the LLM
response text so downstream nodes can access them directly:
- `{{node_id.response}}` -- full raw LLM response (primary access pattern)
- `{{node_id.file_path}}` -- extracted from `**Location:** /path/to/file`
- `{{node_id.file_name}}` -- extracted from `**File:** filename.mp4`
- `{{node_id.url}}` -- extracted from `**URL:** https://...`
- `{{node_id.output_file}}` -- extracted from `**Output:** /path/to/output`

See `AgentNodeOutput` for the full output schema.

**Environment variables** (at least one required):
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — for Claude (primary)
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` — for GPT-4o (fallback)
- `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` + `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` — for Bedrock (fallback)

agent_type.description:
Logical agent type label. All types use direct LLM calls.
Use `"llm"` for general-purpose, or any descriptive label
(e.g., `"assistant"`, `"analyzer"`, `"summarizer"`).

system_prompt.description:
System prompt that sets LLM behavior/persona. Supports {{variable}}
interpolation. If omitted, no system message is sent.

skills.description: Informational only — not used at runtime. Skill names for documentation/profiles.

temperature.description: LLM temperature (0.0 = deterministic, 1.0 = creative). Engine falls back to 0.3 if not set.

max_tokens.description: Maximum tokens in LLM response. Engine falls back to 2000 if not set.

timeout.description: Execution timeout in seconds. Enforced at workflow level via asyncio.wait_for().

auth_token.description: Reserved — not used by agent nodes. Used by other node types (lead, email, etc.).

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata. Stored but not consumed by the agent executor.

action_type.description: Type of action (e.g., send_email, update_database, delay)

method.description: Method to call on the service

parameters.description: Parameters for the action (supports {{template}} variables)

LLMConfig.description:
Configuration for `llm` nodes: one structured completion through Ambivo Core
`POST /genai/complete`, on the tenant's AI setting (see `AgentConfig`).

`prompt` and `system_prompt` are templated. Objects and lists referenced with
`{{node_id.field}}` are inserted as JSON.

With `output_schema`, Core validates the reply and asks again once with the
errors. A reply that still does not match **fails the node**, so
`error_handling` decides what happens next.

**Output:** `{status, node_id, text, data, schema_valid, schema_errors, usage, model}`.
`data` is the parsed JSON reply. Reference it downstream as `{{<node_id>.data.<field>}}`.
The step records `tokens_used`.

Generic by design: a document-reading flow is `ocr` → `llm` (extract to a schema)
→ `validate` → `condition` → a record node, all configured, nothing hardcoded.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema for the reply. A JSON string is accepted (from the designer); blank means unset.

example.prompt:
Extract the bill from this document:
{{ocr.extracted_text}}

ValidateConfig.description:
Configuration for `validate` nodes: checks data from an earlier node against
rules, with no AI call. The node always succeeds; branch on `ok` with a
`condition` node (`expression: "<node_id>.ok"`).

Each rule part (required, type, min, max, pattern, one_of) and each sum check is
one check. `confidence` = passed / checked. `ok` = `confidence >= min_confidence`.
The default `1.0` needs every check to pass. Failed checks are listed in `issues`
either way.

A missing value that is not `required` is skipped. A wrong `type` skips that
field's other checks. Numeric strings such as `"1,200"` count as numbers for
min, max and sums; `type: number` itself is strict.

**Output:** `{status: "success", ok, confidence, issues: [{field, rule, message}],
checked, passed, data}`.

source.description:
Dotted path to the object to check. Looked up in the node's input first, then
across the run, so `"data"` (previous `llm` node) and `"extract.data"` both work.
Unset = the whole input.

min.description: Minimum value, or minimum array length.

max.description: Maximum value, or maximum array length.

pattern.description: Regex, searched. Anchor with ^...$ for a full match.

item_value_key.description: Key inside each item holding the amount.

total_field.description: Dotted path to the stated total.

ConditionConfig.description:
Configuration for condition nodes. Evaluates an expression and routes
to `true_branch` or `false_branch` node.

## Operator vocabulary (exact set the engine recognises)

| Operator                 | Semantics |
|--------------------------|-----------|
| `equals`, `not_equals`   | Compare `expression`-resolved value to `value` |
| `contains`               | `value` is substring of resolved value |
| `greater_than`, `less_than` | Numeric compare (both sides coerced to `float`) |
| `is_empty`, `is_not_empty` | Truthiness check on resolved value |
| `field_update_match`     | AND across pattern fields in `match_updated_fields_dict` (see below) |
| `field_update_match_any` | OR across pattern fields in `match_updated_fields_dict` |
| `match_filter`           | Evaluate Mongo-style `match_filter_dict` (supports `$or`/`$and`/`$not`) |

**Unknown operators** are not silently treated as `False` any more.
As of 2026-05-12 the engine emits a `WARNING` log line listing the
valid set when it receives an operator it does not recognise. The
condition still resolves to `False` (so `false_branch` is taken),
but you will see the warning in server logs.

## Hidden failure mode: downstream pydantic validation cascades back

If a node *downstream* of this condition has invalid config (most
commonly a DELAY with `duration: "{{var}}"` — see
`DelayConfig.duration` warning), the pre-execution pydantic
validation will mark THIS condition's step as `status=failed` with
the downstream node's error in its `error` field. Always inspect
every failed step's `error`, not just the most-recent one, when
debugging.

expression.description: Condition expression or field name to evaluate (used by simple-comparison operators; ignored by field_update_match*/match_filter).

true_branch.description: Node ID to execute when condition is true

false_branch.description: Node ID to execute when condition is false

operator.description:
See "Operator vocabulary" table above. `field_update_match_any`
added 2026-05-12 to express OR semantics across listed fields
without chaining condition nodes. `in`/`not_in` are legacy
aliases kept for back-compat; new workflows should prefer
`match_filter` with `$in`/`$nin`.

before.description: Expected value before update ('*' matches any)

after.description: Expected value after update ('*' matches any)

match_updated_fields.description:
Field update match criteria for automation-migrated conditions.
When set, the condition evaluates whether the specified fields were updated
matching the before/after patterns. Automatically detected — no need to set
operator to `field_update_match` (auto-detect uses AND semantics; set
`operator: field_update_match_any` explicitly to use OR).
Example: `{"stage": {"before": "*", "after": "invoiced"}}`

match_filter_dict.description:
Mongo-style filter dictionary. Used when `operator: "match_filter"`
(or auto-detected when `match_filter_dict` is set).

**Top-level keys are AND'd.** Use logical combinators `$or`, `$and`,
`$not` (added 2026-05-12) for OR / nested logic:

```yaml
match_filter_dict:
  $or:
    - updated_fields_dict.total_amount:     {$exists: true}
    - updated_fields_dict.product_dict_list: {$exists: true}
```

**Per-field operators** ANDed together when supplied as a dict:
`$eq`, `$ne`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$in`, `$nin`,
`$exists`, `$regex`, `$contains`. Bare scalar values are treated
as `$eq`. Field paths support dot-notation
(e.g. `account.address.city`).

Unknown per-field operators log a warning and yield False.
Bad shapes for `$or`/`$and`/`$not` (e.g. `$or` with a non-list
value) log a warning and yield False — they never raise.

metadata.description:
For `field_update_match` / `field_update_match_any`, you MAY put
`match_updated_fields_dict` here as an alternative to the
top-level `match_updated_fields` field. The engine reads both
(top-level wins).

FilterConfig.description: Filters data by field/operator/value. Passes or blocks data flow.

operator.description: Comparison operator: equals, contains, in, not_in, greater_than, less_than

pass_through.description: Whether to pass through if filter matches

LeadConfig.description:
Configuration for lead management nodes. Downstream CRM API patterns:

- `create` → POST `/user/lead` with `{"action": "add", "payload": {...}}`
- `fetch`  → POST `/user/lead` with `{"action": "get", "payload": {"id": "..."}}`
- `update` → POST `/user/lead` with `{"action": "update", "payload": {"id": "...", ...}}`
- `delete` → DELETE `/user/lead?ids_list=["..."]`
- `search` → GET `/user/lead?match_filter_dict=...&page_size=25&skip=0&sort_dict=...`
- `assign` → POST `/user/lead/lead_owner` with `{"lead_id": "...", "new_owner_userid": "..."}`
- `aggregate_report` → POST `/entity/data` with `{"entity_type": "lead", "action": "aggregate_report", ...}` —
  generates an HTML or PDF report combining a group-by (or time-bucket)
  aggregation with a tabular records section. Output exposes
  `report_url`, `report_format`, `report_size_bytes`, `report_summary`
  on the node result so a downstream Email node can interpolate the
  URL via `{{node_id.report_url}}`.

**CRM field normalization:** The execution engine automatically
normalises `email` → `email_list` and `phone` → `phone_list` in
both CREATE and UPDATE payloads, so workflow authors can use either
form interchangeably.

**Ownership:** By default the lead is owned by the user identified by
the auth token. Set `assign_to_userid` to force ownership to a
different user.

template.description: Template for lead data with {{variable}} placeholders

field_mapping.description: Map input fields to API fields (source -> target)

match_filter_dict.description:
MongoDB-style filter — record selector for `search` AND
`aggregate_report` operations. Sent verbatim to the Ambivo
CRM API, which interpolates server-side variables before query:

- `{{current_ts}}` — current epoch seconds (tenant-tz aware)
- `{{yesterday_ts}}`, `{{tomorrow_ts}}`, `{{today}}`
- `expr(<arithmetic>)` — wraps an inline expression that the
  server evaluates to a numeric value, e.g.
  `expr({{current_ts}}-(86400*90))` → epoch 90 days ago.

Workflow-side `{{template_var}}` placeholders (from prior node
outputs or workflow variables) are also interpolated by the
execution engine before the request is sent.

Common patterns:
- `{"lead_status": "qualified"}` — single field
- `{"$and": [{"created_ts": {"$gt": "expr({{current_ts}}-(86400*7))"}}]}` — last 7 days
- `{"lead_source": {"$in": ["{{search_node.source}}", "google"]}}` — workflow-var interpolation
- `{"$or": [{"lead_status": "new"}, {"lead_status": "contacted"}]}` — multi-status

assign_to_userid.description:
Force lead ownership to this user ID instead of the authenticated
user. Maps to the Ambivo API's `assign_to_userid` payload field.
When omitted, the lead is owned by the user identified by the
auth token.

group_by_fields.description:
Fields to group on (e.g. `["lead_status"]`). Required for
`aggregate_report` unless `date_field`+`time_grain` are provided.

aggregate_field.description: Numeric field to sum/avg, defaults to count.

report_upload_to_s3.description: When `true`, response includes presigned S3 URL; else inline content.

include_records.description: Include tabular records list under the aggregate.

record_limit.description: Cap (server enforces hard max 1000). Set 0 to skip records.

entity_ids_list.description:
Explicit ID list — alternative or addition to `match_filter_dict`.
Supports `{{template_var}}` interpolation (resolves to a list or
comma-separated string).

AccountConfig.description:
Configuration for account management nodes. Same action-based POST pattern as Lead.

- `create` → POST `/user/customer/account` with `{"action": "add", "payload": {...}}`
- `fetch`  → POST `/user/customer/account` with `{"action": "get", "account_id": "..."}`
- `update` → POST `/user/customer/account` with `{"action": "update", "account_id": "...", "payload": {...}}`
- `delete` → DELETE `/user/customer/account?ids_list=["..."]`
- `search` → GET `/user/customer/account?match_filter_dict=...&page_size=25&skip=0&sort_dict=...`
- `aggregate_report` → POST `/entity/data` with `{"entity_type": "account", "action": "aggregate_report", ...}` —
  see LeadConfig.aggregate_report for full semantics.

**CRM field normalization:** `email` → `email_list` and
`phone` → `phone_list` are auto-normalised in CREATE and UPDATE
payloads.

assign_to_userid.description:
Force account ownership to this user ID instead of the
authenticated user.

Implemented email operations:
- `send` — Send email with template_variables (to, subject, body)
- `send_template` — Send using a template_id with variables

Not yet implemented: `schedule`, `fetch`, `reply`

EmailConfig.description:
Configuration for email nodes. Supports two patterns:
1. **template_variables** — generic `to`/`subject`/`body` keys in a dict
2. **Direct fields** — `to_list`, `message_subject`, `message_body`, `sender_name`, `sender_email`
   (preferred for automation-migrated workflows)

template_variables.description:
Variables for the email. For send operation, can include:
- `to` (string): Recipient email
- `subject` (string): Email subject
- `body` (string): Email body (HTML supported)

sender_email.description: Sender email address (used as from_address if from_address is not set)

auth_token.description: Node-level Bearer token override; falls back to workflow-level authorization_token

EmailReaderOperations.description:
Implemented: `search` — searches IMAP mailbox with criteria and prev_mins filter.
Not yet implemented: `fetch_messages`, `read_message`, `mark_as_read`, `mark_as_unread`, `invoke_api`

prev_mins.description: Filter emails from last N minutes (0 = disabled)

Implemented: `fetch_raw_batch` — fetches raw email content for all UIDs from email_reader output.
Not yet implemented: `fetch_raw`, `parse_headers`, `extract_content`, `invoke_api`

EmailRawReaderConfig.description: Configuration for raw email content reader nodes

YelpLeadReplyOperations.description:
Implemented: `process_batch` (batch email processing), `process_lead` (single email).
Not yet implemented: `extract_only`, `reply_only`, `invoke_api`

YelpLeadReplyConfig.description: Configuration for Yelp lead AI reply nodes

APICallConfig.description:
Configuration for generic HTTP API call nodes.
Accepts `url` or `api_url` (alias), and `body_template` or `request_body` (alias).

http_method.description: Redundant with operation; accepted for automation-migration compatibility

response_mapping.description: Map response fields to output keys

response_schema.description:
Describe expected API response fields for the workflow designer.
Keys are field names, values are types (string, number, integer, boolean, array, object).
Example: {"price": "number", "symbol": "string", "volume": "integer"}
The designer uses this to show available {{node_id.result.field}} references
for downstream nodes. Not used by the execution engine.

DelayConfig.description:
Configuration for delay/wait nodes. Two mutually exclusive modes:
- **Fixed delay:** set `duration` + `unit` (e.g. 60 days).
- **Dynamic delay:** set `target_timestamp` (template string resolving to Unix epoch)
  with optional `offset_seconds` subtracted before computing delay.
  Example: `target_timestamp: "{{order_line_list.0.renewal_date}}"`, `offset_seconds: 6480000`
  means "wait until 75 days before the renewal date".
Exactly one of `duration` or `target_timestamp` must be provided.
Short delays (≤ CELERY_DELAY_THRESHOLD) use asyncio.sleep.
Long delays are scheduled via Celery ETA.

duration.description:
Fixed delay duration in the specified `unit` (mutually exclusive with `target_timestamp`).

**CRITICAL: NOT interpolatable.** Must be a literal integer.
Saving `"{{some_var}}"` here will fail Pydantic validation at
workflow execution time with:
`1 validation error for DelayConfig — duration: Input should be a valid integer`.

**Diagnostic gotcha:** the validation failure cascades back to the
PRECEDING condition step — that condition's step record will be
marked `status=failed` with the DelayConfig pydantic error in
its `error` field, NOT the delay step. So if you see a condition
step failing with a DelayConfig error, check the delay node
config, not the condition.

target_timestamp.description:
Template string that resolves to a Unix epoch timestamp (seconds).
Supports {{expression}} interpolation from workflow data.
Mutually exclusive with `duration`.

**Interpolation surface:** `target_timestamp` IS interpolated by
the engine before evaluation. `offset_seconds` (below), `duration`,
and `jitter` are NOT — they must be literal integers in the saved
workflow.

offset_seconds.description:
Seconds to subtract from `target_timestamp` before computing delay
(e.g. `6480000` = 75 days BEFORE target; `-5184000` = 60 days
AFTER target — negative offset adds).

**NOT interpolatable.** This field is typed `int` and the engine
does NOT run template substitution on it. `"{{some_var}}"` saved
here will crash at execution with `float - str` TypeError when
the delay is computed. To parameterize the delay window, edit
this literal value after import (or fork the template).

cron_expression.description: Cron expression for complex scheduling (overrides interval)

NotificationConfig.description:
Configuration for notification nodes. Calls the holistic notification
endpoint `POST /user/notifications/manage` which supports in-app,
push (FCM), WebSocket, email, and SMS delivery in a single call.

**Channel control:** Use `send_push_notification`, `send_socket`, and
`send_third_party_apps` booleans for core channels. Set `email_config`
and/or `sms_config` objects to enable those channels alongside push/socket.

**Scheduling:** Set `initial_delay > 60` seconds to queue the notification
for deferred delivery via TenantScheduledTask.

**Auth token resolution:** node auth_token > workflow authorization_token > execution context JWT.

api_url.description: Holistic notification endpoint. Override for custom notification services.

auth_token.description: Node-level Bearer token override. Supports {{variable}} interpolation.

message_title.description: Notification title. Maps to holistic endpoint 'title' field.

message_body.description: Notification body text. Required by holistic endpoint.

userid.description: Target user ID. Maps to 'for_userid'. If omitted, sends to the caller.

message_data.description: Arbitrary data payload (list of dicts) attached to the notification.

send_third_party_apps.description: Enable third-party app notifications like Connecteam (channels.third_party_apps).

email_config.description:
Optional email channel configuration. Set to enable email delivery alongside push/socket.
Fields: `recipient_list` (array of emails, required), `subject` (string),
`sender_email` (string), `sender_name` (string).
All fields support {{variable}} interpolation.

subject.description: Email subject. Defaults to message_title if omitted.

sender_email.description: Sender email. If it matches an authorized mailbox, sent via that mailbox.

sms_config.description:
Optional SMS channel configuration. Set to enable SMS delivery alongside push/socket.
All fields support {{variable}} interpolation.

text.description: SMS text. Defaults to message_body if omitted.

initial_delay.description: Delay in seconds before delivery. If >60, notification is queued for deferred delivery.

collapse_key.description: FCM collapse key for notification coalescing.

notification_image.description: Image URL for push notification. Supports {{variable}} interpolation.

TaskOperations.description:
Implemented task operations:
- `create` — POST /user_tasks (create a new task)
- `update` — PATCH /user_tasks/{task_id} (update task fields)
- `fetch` — GET /user_tasks/{task_id} (get task by ID)
- `search` — GET /user_tasks (list/filter/sort tasks with pagination)

Not yet implemented: `delete`, `assign`

TaskConfig.description:
Configuration for task management nodes. Uses the CRM REST API at `/user_tasks`.

**Per-operation input fields:**

| Operation | Required Fields | Optional Fields |
|-----------|----------------|-----------------|
| `create` | `task_name`, **`due_date`** | `description`, `priority`, `action`, `status`, `userid`, `due_date_offset_seconds`, `notifications_on`, `create_cal_event`, `subject_type`, `subject`, `tags`, `meta`, `comments` |
| `update` | `task_id` (or from input_data) | `task_name`, `description`, `priority`, `status`, `due_date`, `userid` |
| `fetch` | `task_id` (or from input_data) | — |
| `search` | GET `/user_tasks` | `match_filter_dict`, `page_size`, `skip`, `sort_dict` |

> **`due_date` is REQUIRED for `create`.** The upstream Ambivo
> `/user_tasks` endpoint rejects `create` calls without a `due_date`
> with a `VALIDATION_ERROR`. The executor short-circuits with a clear
> error if `due_date` is empty, so no upstream call is made. Provide
> an epoch-seconds timestamp (string) or a template expression like
> `{{ now + 86400 }}` (24 hours from now). The designer's default
> template for the `task` node uses `{{ now + 86400 }}`.

**Ambivo `result: 2` failure pattern:** `/user_tasks` (and other
Ambivo CRM endpoints) may return HTTP 200 with `result: 2` and
`error_code: VALIDATION_ERROR` to signal failure. The executor
recognises this pattern and returns `status: "error"` at the node
level — the workflow execution will be marked failed, and the
upstream `error.message` is surfaced in `step.error` plus the full
body in `step.error_detail`.

**Per-operation output:**

| Operation | Output Keys |
|-----------|------------|
| `create` | `status`, `operation`, `node_id`, `task_created`, `result`, `status_code` |
| `update` | `status`, `operation`, `node_id`, `task_updated`, `result`, `status_code` |
| `fetch` | `status`, `operation`, `node_id`, `result`, `status_code` |
| `search` | `status`, `operation`, `node_id`, `result` (contains `data[]`, `total_count`), `status_code` |

api_url.description: CRM Task REST API. Uses standard HTTP methods (POST/PATCH/GET), not action-based pattern.

task_id.description: Task ID for update/fetch operations. Supports {{variable}} interpolation. Falls back to input_data.task_id.

task_name.description: Task title (required for create, optional for update).

priority.description: Mapped to API integers: high=1, medium=2, low=3.

action.description: Task action type: general, call, email, text, postcard, support-request, work-order, attend-meeting, renewal-reminder.

status.description: Task status: assigned, in-progress, rejected, reviewsubmit, reviewpass, completed.

due_date.description:
**REQUIRED for `create`.** Epoch-seconds timestamp (string) or
template expression like `{{ now + 86400 }}` (24h from now).
The Ambivo /user_tasks endpoint rejects create requests
without this field.

due_date_offset_minutes.description: Minutes from now for due date calculation.

due_date_offset_seconds.description: Seconds to subtract from the resolved `due_date` value. Use to schedule tasks relative to a future date (e.g. 6480000 = 75 days before renewal_date).

create_cal_event.description: When true, creates a Google Calendar event on the assigned user's default calendar at the task due date.

subject_type.description: Entity type the task relates to.

subject.description: Entity ID the task relates to. Supports {{variable}} interpolation.

tags.description: Tags for the task. Each tag supports {{variable}} interpolation.

meta.description: Arbitrary metadata dict. Values support {{variable}} interpolation.

comments.description: HTML comments to attach to the task. Supports {{variable}} interpolation.

match_filter_dict.description: MongoDB-style filter for search operation. E.g. {"status": "assigned", "priority": 1}.

TaskSequenceConfig.description: Configuration for task sequence nodes (create tasks from templates)

user_task_sequence_id.description: ID of the task sequence template

CampaignConfig.description:
Configuration for campaign membership nodes. All operations use action-based POST.

- `add_member` → POST `/campaign_member/manage` with `{"action": "add", ...}`
- `remove_member` → POST `/campaign_member/manage` with `{"action": "delete", ...}`
- `update_member` → POST `/campaign_member/manage` with `{"action": "update", ...}`
- `fetch_members` → POST `/campaign_member/manage` with `{"action": "get", ...}`

invoice_id.description: Ambivo invoice id that was pushed

qb_invoice_id.description:
QuickBooks `Invoice.Id` returned by QB. Nullable only when the QB
response JSON could not be parsed for an id; the create still
succeeded on QB's side in that case.

response.description: Raw QB Invoice payload returned by Intuit

error_code.description:
Canonical error code for clients that prefer `error_code` over
`reason`. Always equals `reason` when both are present.

qb_invoice_id.description:
Populated only on `INVOICE_ALREADY_EXPORTED` (the existing QB
invoice id the caller should `/sync` against instead).

msg.description: Human-readable detail (present on SERIALIZE_ERROR and QB_CREATE_FAILED)

error.description: Inner Intuit error dict (present on QB_CREATE_FAILED)

bill_id.description: Ambivo bill id that was pushed

qb_bill_id.description:
QuickBooks `Bill.Id` returned by QB. Nullable only when the QB
response JSON could not be parsed for an id; the create still
succeeded on QB's side in that case.

response.description: Raw QB Bill payload returned by Intuit

error_code.description:
Canonical error code for clients that prefer `error_code` over
`reason`. Always equals `reason` when both are present.

qb_bill_id.description:
Populated when the bill is already exported and the caller should
update the existing QB bill instead.

msg.description: Human-readable detail (present on SERIALIZE_ERROR and QB_CREATE_FAILED/QB_UPDATE_FAILED)

error.description: Inner Intuit error dict (present on QB_CREATE_FAILED/QB_UPDATE_FAILED)

reason.description:
Canonical outcome/reason code. `COMMISSION_BILL_DISABLED` when
`tenant.commission_bill_enabled` is off; `ORDER_NOT_FOUND` when the
order does not exist for this tenant.

order_id.description: Ambivo order id whose commission bills were reconciled

InvoiceConfig.description:
Configuration for invoice management nodes. Action-based POST pattern.

- `create/fetch/update/delete` → POST `/user/invoice` with `{"action": "add|get|update|delete", ...}`
- `create_intuit` → POST `/intuit/invoice/{invoice_id}/create_intuit`
  (dedicated CRM endpoint; no request body required — `realm_id` is
  auto-resolved from the tenant's `intuit_profile`). The node reads
  `invoice_id` from `config.invoice_id` (with `{{ invoice_id }}`
  interpolation against the trigger event payload) or falls back to
  `input_data['invoice_id']`. See path
  `/intuit/invoice/{invoice_id}/create_intuit` for response shape and
  reason codes. Refuses safely on re-fires (`409
  INVOICE_ALREADY_EXPORTED`).
- `search` → GET `/user/invoice?match_filter_dict=...&page_size=25&skip=0&sort_dict=...`

create_data.description: Complete invoice payload for create operations

BillConfig.description:
Configuration for bill (accounts-payable) management nodes. Bill is the
A/P counterpart of Invoice. Action-based POST pattern.

- `create/fetch/update/delete` → POST `/user/bill/manage` with `{"action": "add|get|update|delete", "payload": {...}}`
- `create_intuit` → POST `/intuit/bill/{bill_id}/create_intuit`
  (dedicated CRM endpoint; no request body required — `realm_id` is
  auto-resolved from the tenant's `intuit_profile`). The node reads
  `bill_id` from `config.bill_id` (with `{{ bill_id }}`
  interpolation against the trigger event payload) or falls back to
  `input_data['bill_id']`. The Bill must carry a resolved
  `source_vendor_ref_dict`. See path
  `/intuit/bill/{bill_id}/create_intuit` for response shape and
  reason codes. If the Bill is already exported the endpoint performs a
  SyncToken sparse-update instead of a create.
- `reconcile_commission_bills` → POST `/intuit/order/{order_id}/reconcile_commission_bills`
  (reconciles salesperson-commission Bills for one order; see that path).
- `search` → GET `/user/bill/manage?match_filter_dict=...&page_size=25&skip=0&sort_dict=...`

create_data.description: Complete bill payload for create operations

order_id.description: For commission-bill reconciliation from an order

expense_account_id.description: Ledger account the bill is booked to (e.g. tenant.commission_expense_account_id)

source_vendor_ref_dict.description: QuickBooks vendor reference (required to push to QB)

OpportunityConfig.description:
Configuration for opportunity management nodes. Action-based POST pattern.

- `create/fetch/update` → POST `/user/opportunity` with `{"action": "add|get|update", ...}`
- `delete` → DELETE `/user/opportunity?ids_list=["..."]`
- `search` → GET `/user/opportunity?match_filter_dict=...&page_size=25&skip=0&sort_dict=...`
- `aggregate_report` → POST `/entity/data` with `{"entity_type": "opportunity", "action": "aggregate_report", ...}` —
  see LeadConfig.aggregate_report for full semantics.

create_data.description: Complete opportunity payload for create operations

UpdateRecordConfig.description: Configuration for generic record update nodes

entity_type.description: Entity type: lead, contact, order, etc.
Entity type: lead, contact, order, etc.

TranscribeConfig.description:
Configuration for transcribe nodes. Calls vectordb-api POST /kh/transcribe endpoint.
Converts audio/video files to text using AWS Transcribe.

**Auth token resolution order:**
1. Node-level `auth_token` (highest priority, supports {{variable}} interpolation)
2. Workflow-level `authorization_token`
3. Execution context JWT (from trigger/caller)

**Environment variable:** `VECTORDB_API_URL` (default: https://vectordbapi.ambivo.com)

auth_token.description: Node-level auth token. Overrides workflow-level token. Supports {{variable}} interpolation.

s3_url.description: S3 URL of audio/video file. Supports {{variable}} interpolation.

file_url.description: Public URL of audio/video file. Supports {{variable}} interpolation.

poll_interval.description: Status polling interval in seconds when job is pending.

TranscribeNodeOutput.description:
Output from a transcribe node. Top-level fields are flattened for easy
downstream access via `{{node_id.transcribed_content}}`, etc.

The `result` field contains the full vectordb-api response object,
which includes the raw AWS Transcribe output with word-level items,
audio segments, and speaker labels. UI consumers should use the
top-level fields for display and only dig into `result` for advanced
features (e.g. word-level timestamps).

transcribed_content.description: Full transcribed text — primary field for downstream use.

region.description: AWS region where the job ran (e.g. 'us-east-1').

result.description:
Full vectordb-api response. Contains the same top-level fields plus:
- `s3_url` (string): S3 URI of the uploaded audio file
- `message` (string): Human-readable status message
- `transcription_result` (object): Raw AWS Transcribe output including:
  - `transcribed_content` (string): Same as top-level
  - `transcribed_dict` (object): Full AWS response with `results.items` (word-level
    with timestamps and confidence) and `results.audio_segments` (segment-level)
  - `completion_status` (string): "COMPLETED"
  - `s3_url`, `job_name`, `region`

**Note for UI:** The `transcribed_dict.results.items` array can contain 1000+
entries (one per word). Use top-level `transcribed_content` for display;
only access `result.transcription_result.transcribed_dict` for word-level
timestamps or confidence scores.

OCRConfig.description:
Configuration for OCR nodes. Calls vectordb-api POST /kh/ocr endpoint.
Extracts text from images and documents using AWS Textract.

**Auth token resolution:** Same as TranscribeConfig (node > workflow > context).

**Supported formats:** jpg, jpeg, png, pdf, tiff, tif, bmp

auth_token.description: Node-level auth token. Overrides workflow-level token.

OCRNodeOutput.description:
Output from an OCR node. Top-level fields are flattened for easy
downstream access via `{{node_id.extracted_text}}`, etc.

The `result` field contains the full vectordb-api response object,
which includes the raw AWS Textract output. UI consumers should use
the top-level fields for display and only dig into `result` for
advanced features (e.g. bounding boxes, table cell data).

extracted_text.description: Full extracted text — primary field for downstream use.

items.description:
Each entry has `type` ("form_field", "table", or "query_result").
- form_field: `key`, `value`, `confidence`
- table: `data` (2D array of cell strings), `confidence`
- query_result: `text`, `confidence`

extracted_data.description: Structured data (forms/tables/queries) if requested via form_document, extract_tables, or extract_queries config.

region.description: AWS region where the Textract job ran (e.g. 'us-east-1').

s3_url.description: S3 URL of the uploaded file that was processed.

result.description:
Full vectordb-api response. Contains:
- `result` (integer): 1 for success, 2 for error
- `message` (string): Human-readable status message
- `ocr_result` (object): Detailed Textract output including:
  - `status` ("SUCCESS"/"FAILED")
  - `extracted_text`, `extracted_data` (same as top-level)
  - `block_count` (integer): Number of Textract blocks processed
  - `processing_timestamp` (number): Unix timestamp
  - `processing_method` ("direct_bytes"/"s3_redirect")
- Plus copies of `extracted_text`, `extracted_data`, `text_length`,
  `data_count`, `job_id`, `region`, `s3_url`, `processing_type`

**Note for UI:** Use top-level fields for display. Only access
`result.ocr_result` for raw Textract data like block counts or
processing metadata.

SMSConfig.description:
Configuration for SMS nodes. Sends SMS via Ambivo telephony API.
All string fields support `{{template}}` variable interpolation.

ContactConfig.description:
Configuration for Contact nodes. Same Ambivo action-based POST pattern as Lead.

- `create/fetch/update` → POST `/user/contact` with `{"action": "add|get|update", ...}`
- `delete` → DELETE `/user/contact?ids_list=["..."]`
- `search` → GET `/user/contact?match_filter_dict=...&page_size=25&skip=0&sort_dict=...`
- `aggregate_report` → POST `/entity/data` with `{"entity_type": "contact", "action": "aggregate_report", ...}` —
  see LeadConfig.aggregate_report for full semantics.

**CRM field normalization:** `email` → `email_list` and
`phone` → `phone_list` are auto-normalised in CREATE and UPDATE
payloads.

assign_to_userid.description:
Force contact ownership to this user ID instead of the
authenticated user.

OrderConfig.description:
Configuration for Order nodes. Same Ambivo action-based POST pattern as Lead.

- `create/fetch/update` → POST `/user/order` with `{"action": "add|get|update", ...}`
- `delete` → DELETE `/user/order?ids_list=["..."]`
- `search` → GET `/user/order?match_filter_dict=...&page_size=25&skip=0&sort_dict=...`

CustomObjectConfig.description:
Configuration for the generic **Custom Object** node (`type: "custom_object"`).

A single node type serves EVERY custom object (custom module) — the target
is selected via `collection_id` (the bare collection id, e.g. `support_tickets`,
NOT the canonical `amb_<tenant>_<id>`). Unlike the per-entity nodes which use
the action-based `/user/{entity}` contract, custom objects are REST:

- `create` → POST `/custom/object/data` with `{"collection_id", "data": {...}}`
- `update` → PUT `/custom/object/data` with `{"collection_id", "id", "data": {...}}`
- `delete` → DELETE `/custom/object/data` with `{"collection_id", "id"}` or
  `{"collection_id", "action": "delete_many", "ids_list": [...]}`
- `fetch`  → GET `/custom/object/data?collection_id=...&action=get&id=...`
- `search` → GET `/custom/object/data?collection_id=...&action=get&match_filter_dict=...`

**Filter targeting (canonical match):** for `update`/`delete`, when `record_id`
is omitted the engine resolves target id(s) from `match_filter_dict` via a fetch
first. `apply_to_all_matches=false` (default) touches only the first match.

**Loop safety:** workflow-initiated writes send `suppress_automation_triggers=true`
so the write does not re-publish a custom-object event.

The per-object FIELD schema is dynamic (per tenant); fetch it via
`GET /custom/object/data?action=get_schema&collection_id=...` (designer renders
the field form from it). Custom-object events (`{collection_id}.create|update|delete`)
fire workflows through the same EventBus path as standard entities.

collection_id.description: Bare custom-object collection id (e.g. support_tickets). Required for all operations.

match_filter_dict.description:
MongoDB-style filter. For search: the query. For update/delete: resolves
target record id(s) when record_id is omitted.

apply_to_all_matches.description: When matching by filter, act on every match instead of just the first.

x-node-output-schemas.description:
## Node Output Shapes

Every node execution returns a dict stored under `node_outputs[node_id]`.
Downstream nodes access fields via `{{node_id.field}}` or `{{node_id.result.nested_field}}`.

### CRM Entity Nodes (Lead, Contact, Account, Order, Opportunity, Invoice)

All CRM entities follow the same Ambivo action-based API response pattern:

| Operation | Output Fields | Key Reference |
|-----------|--------------|---------------|
| **create** | `status`, `operation`, `node_id`, `result.result` (1=success), `result.data.id` (created record ID) | `{{node_id.result.data.id}}` |
| **search** | `status`, `operation`, `node_id`, `result.result`, `result.data` (array of records), `result.gross_count` (total) | `{{node_id.result.data}}` |
| **update** | `status`, `operation`, `node_id`, `result.result` (1=success) | `{{node_id.result.result}}` |
| **fetch** | `status`, `operation`, `node_id`, `result.result`, `result.data` (full record object) | `{{node_id.result.data}}` |
| **delete** | `status`, `operation`, `node_id`, `result.result` (1=success) | `{{node_id.result.result}}` |

Lead also supports: `assign` (returns updated lead), `convert` (returns `result.data.id` = new opportunity ID)

### Agent Node

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `status` | string | "success" or "failed" |
| `response` | string | Agent's full markdown response |
| `agent_type` | string | e.g. "assistant", "youtube_download" |
| `file_path` | string? | Extracted from **Location:** in response |
| `file_name` | string? | Extracted from **File:** |
| `url` | string? | Extracted from **URL:** |
| `output_file` | string? | Extracted from **Output:** |

Reference: `{{node_id.response}}`, `{{node_id.file_path}}`

### Email Node

| Operation | Output | Reference |
|-----------|--------|-----------|
| send | `status`, `operation`, `node_id`, `result.status`, `result.to` | `{{node_id.result.status}}` |
| send_template | `status`, `result.status` | `{{node_id.result.status}}` |

### SMS Node

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `status` | string | "success" |
| `to_number` | string | Recipient phone |
| `result.result` | integer | 1 = queued |
| `result.response` | string | "message_queued" |

### Notification Node

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `status` | string | "success" or "error" |
| `notification_sent` | boolean | Delivery success |
| `channels` | object | Per-channel delivery status |
| `notification_id` | string | Notification ID |

### API Call Node

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `status` | string | "success" |
| `operation` | string | HTTP method used |
| `result` | object | API response body |

For third-party APIs, use `response_schema` in the config to describe
expected response fields. The designer shows these as available references.

### Condition Node

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `condition_result` | boolean | true or false |
| `branch_taken` | string | "true_branch" or "false_branch" |
| *(+ all input_data fields)* | | Pass-through |

### Email Processing Pipeline

**Email Reader** (search): `email_list_summary` (array), `all_uid_list` (array), `total_messages` (integer)
**Email Raw Reader**: `raw_emails` (array), `total_processed`, `successful`, `failed`
**Yelp Lead Reply**: `processed_emails` (array), `total_processed`

### Media Nodes

**Transcribe**: `transcribed_content` (string), `content_length`, `job_name`, `region`
**OCR**: `extracted_text` (string), `extracted_data` (array), `text_length`, `data_count`, `job_id`

### Scheduling Nodes

**Appointment/Task/Task Sequence**: `status`, `operation`, `node_id`, `result` (full API response), `status_code`
Task operations also include: `task_created`, `task_updated`, `task_deleted`, `task_assigned`, `assigned_to`

### Campaign Node

All operations return: `status`, `operation`, `node_id`, `result`, `status_code`

WorkflowEvent.description:
A durable record in the `workflow_events` collection representing an
entity event that was received, queued, and (eventually) processed
by the workflow execution engine.

workflow_id.description: Resolved at ingestion. Null if no matching workflow or lookup failed.

execution_id.description: Populated when the consumer creates a workflow execution

status.description:
- **pending** — waiting for consumer pickup
- **claimed** — consumer is processing
- **completed** — workflow executed successfully
- **failed** — transient failure, will retry after `next_retry_at`
- **dead_letter** — retries exhausted or permanent failure
- **skipped** — no matching workflow at ingestion time

attempt_count.description: Number of processing attempts so far

max_retries.description: Maximum retries before moving to dead_letter

next_retry_at.description: Exponential backoff target for next retry

claimed_by.description: Hostname of the worker that claimed this event

error_history.description: History of processing errors (capped at 50 entries)

ExecutionListResponse.description: Paginated execution list response (follows Ambivo entity/data paradigm)

event_id.description:
Link to the originating event in the `workflow_events`
collection. Present when the execution was triggered
via the persistent event queue.

error.description:
Human-readable failure reason, formatted as
`"<primary message> (HTTP <status>, <node_type>.<operation>)"`.
For Ambivo `result: 2` failures (HTTP 200 with
an `error_code`/`error.message` body), the
primary message is mined from `error.message`.
Empty/null when the step succeeded.

error_detail.description:
Raw upstream API response body when the step
failed at an HTTP/API call. Lets the UI render
the full server response (e.g., validation
details, error_code, request_path) without
truncation. Null when the step succeeded or
when no response body was captured.

status_code.description:
HTTP status code from the downstream API call
for failed steps that came from an HTTP
invocation (e.g., 400, 422, 500). Stored
separately from `output_data` for easy
badge rendering in the executions UI. Null
for non-HTTP node types or successful steps.

zombie_retry_count.description: Number of automatic retries dispatched by the zombie reaper

zombie_retried_at.description: When the last automatic retry was dispatched

manual_replay.description: Set to true when replayed via scripts/replay_zombie_executions.py

total_count.description: Number of records in this page

gross_count.description: Total matching records across all pages

skip_num.description: Effective skip (either supplied `skip_num` or computed from page_num/page_size).

These are aspirational defaults only. For AI agents, use `type: "agent"` with `AgentConfig`.

WorkflowTemplateSummary.description: Summary of a workflow template for the catalog listing.

template_id.description: Filename stem — used as path param for GET/POST template endpoints.

name.example: Weekly Lead Aggregate Report — Email Digest

node_types.description: Unique node types used in this template, in order of first appearance.

has_triggers.description: True if the template defines scheduled/webhook triggers.

variables.description: Variable names the template expects. Pass these in the create endpoint's overrides.

TemplateCreateOverrides.description:
Optional overrides when creating a workflow from a template.
All fields are optional — omit to use template defaults.

**Important:** Workflows created from templates default to
`status="draft"` and `enabled=false` so a tenant can review and
adjust nodes/variables/triggers before activation. Pass
`{"status": "active", "enabled": true}` to skip the draft step
when seeding programmatically.

name.description: Override the workflow name. If omitted, uses the template's name.

variables.description:
Merge with template variables. Keys in this dict override
matching template variable keys. Non-matching template keys are preserved.

authorization_token.description: Set the workflow-level auth token. Inherited by nodes that don't set their own.

enabled.description:
Whether the workflow is enabled for execution. **Defaults to
`false`** so the imported workflow lands in draft. Set to `true`
(along with `status: active`) to make it run immediately.

status.description:
Initial workflow status. **Defaults to `draft`** — tenant must
explicitly activate via `PUT /api/workflows/{workflow_id}` (or
override here at create time).

TriggerNodeOutput.description:
Output from a trigger node. Trigger nodes are **pass-through** — they
return `trigger_data` unchanged as their output. This means the trigger
node's output IS the `trigger_data` dict from the execution request.

The shape depends on how the workflow was started. There are two
construction patterns:

**Pattern A — `TriggerBase.fire()` envelope** (webhook, schedule,
email, conversation, form_submit, database_change):
```
trigger_id, trigger_type, trigger_name, timestamp, data, metadata
```

**Pattern B — direct construction** (event, manual, file_upload, api_call):
Each builds its own shape (see table below).

| Trigger type | Schema | Envelope | Key fields in output |
|---|---|---|---|
| **manual** | `TriggerOutputManual` | None — raw caller dict | Whatever the caller sends in `trigger_data` |
| **api_call** | `TriggerOutputApiCall` | None — raw caller dict | Same as manual (bypass fire()) |
| **event** | `TriggerOutputEntityCreated/Updated/Deleted/Assigned/Converted` | Custom (not fire()) | `trigger_type`, `tenant_id`, `triggered_by_userid`, `trigger_id`, `trigger_name`, `timestamp`, `data`, `metadata` |
| **schedule** | `TriggerOutputSchedule` | fire() | `trigger_id`, `trigger_type`, `trigger_name`, `timestamp`, `data.scheduled_time`, `metadata` |
| **webhook** | `TriggerOutputWebhook` | fire() | `trigger_id`, `trigger_type`, `trigger_name`, `timestamp`, `data` (POST body + `_webhook_meta`), `metadata` |
| **file_upload** | `TriggerOutputFileUpload` | None — flat dict | `file_id`, `original_name`, `filename`, `file_url`, `file_path`, `size`, `mime_type`, `uploaded_at`, `event_type` |
| **email** | `TriggerOutputEmail` | fire() | `trigger_id`, `trigger_type`, `trigger_name`, `timestamp`, `data` (from email monitor), `metadata` |
| **form_submit** | `TriggerOutputFormSubmit` | fire() | `trigger_id`, `trigger_type`, `trigger_name`, `timestamp`, `data` (form fields), `metadata` |
| **conversation** | `TriggerOutputConversation` | fire() | `trigger_id`, `trigger_type`, `trigger_name`, `timestamp`, `data` (conversation context), `metadata` |
| **database_change** | `TriggerOutputDatabaseChange` | fire() | `trigger_id`, `trigger_type`, `trigger_name`, `timestamp`, `data` (same as entity events), `metadata` |

**Downstream access patterns:**
- Flat: `{{field}}` — resolves from the trigger output (immediate parent)
- Namespaced: `{{trigger_node.field}}` — resolves from `node_outputs`

**Event flattening:** For entity events, the execution engine flattens
`data.instance_payload` fields into the execution context, so downstream
nodes can use `{{lead_status}}` instead of `{{data.instance_payload.lead_status}}`.

**Key difference — event vs fire() triggers:** Event triggers (built in
`workflow_tasks.py`) include `tenant_id` and `triggered_by_userid` at the
top level. Triggers using the `TriggerBase.fire()` factory do NOT include
these fields — they only have `trigger_id`, `trigger_type`, `trigger_name`,
`timestamp`, `data`, and `metadata`.

**Note:** The properties below describe the fire() envelope and event
trigger fields. Manual, api_call, and file_upload triggers have different
shapes — see their dedicated schemas. All properties are optional because
the shape varies by trigger type.

trigger_type.description: Present on fire() and event triggers. Values: 'event', 'schedule', 'webhook', 'email', 'conversation', 'form_submit', 'database_change'. NOT present on manual/api_call/file_upload.

trigger_name.description: For event triggers: composite event name (e.g. 'lead.created'). For fire() triggers: config name.

trigger_id.description: UUID. Present on fire() triggers and event triggers.

tenant_id.description: **Event triggers only.** Tenant ID from the event. NOT present on fire() triggers.

triggered_by_userid.description: **Event triggers only.** User who caused the event. NOT present on fire() triggers.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. Present on fire() and event triggers.

data.description: Payload. Shape varies by trigger type — see per-type schemas.

metadata.description: From trigger config metadata. Present on fire() and event triggers (usually empty).

AgentNodeOutput.description:
Output from an `agent` node (direct LLM call).

**Fixed fields** (always present):
- `status` — `"success"` or `"failed"`
- `response` — full raw LLM response text
- `agent_type` — the `agent_type` label from config
- `node_id` — the node's ID

**On failure**, `error` contains the first 500 chars of the error response.

**Structured field extraction** (optional, added when patterns match):
The engine parses markdown patterns from the LLM response to populate
extra fields. Downstream nodes access them via `{{node_id.field}}`.

| Field | Extracted from | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `file_path` | `**Location:** /path` or `**Output:** {final_path: ...}` | `/shared/audio.mp3` |
| `file_name` | `**File:** name` or `**Output:** {filename: ...}` | `report.pdf` |
| `file_type` | `**Type:** value` | `Video (MP4)` |
| `file_size` | `**Size:** value` or `**Output:** {size_bytes: ...}` | `16.08 MB` |
| `url` | `**URL:** value` or first `https://` in response | `https://example.com` |
| `download_time` | `**Download Time:** value` | `5.37s` |
| `output_file` | `**Output:** value` (raw string) | `{'filename': 'out.mp4', ...}` |

**Fallback extraction:**
- If no `file_path` found via markdown, the engine extracts the last absolute
  file path matching common extensions (mp4, mp3, pdf, csv, etc.) from the response.
- If no `url` found via `**URL:**`, the engine extracts the first `https://` URL.

**Side effect:** The raw `response` string is also stored in the execution
variables as `agent_response` for legacy `{{agent_response}}` access.

response.description: Full raw text response from the LLM.

error.description: Present only when status is 'failed'. First 500 chars of the error response.

file_path.description: Extracted from **Location:** or **Output:** dict's final_path/path, or last absolute file path in response.

file_size.description: Extracted from **Size:** or **Output:** dict's size_bytes (as string).

url.description: Extracted from **URL:** or first https:// URL in response.

output_file.description: Raw value from **Output:** line — may be a path string or a Python dict literal.

AppointmentInputSchema.description: Default input schema for appointment nodes

AppointmentNodeOutput.description:
Output from an appointment node. Fields vary by operation:

| Operation | Key Fields |
|-----------|-----------|
| `create` | `appointment_created: true`, `result: {result: 1, response_dict: {id, htmlLink}}` |
| `update` | `appointment_updated: true`, `result: {result: 1, response_dict: {...}}` |
| `fetch` | `result: {calendar events data}` |

appointment_created.description: Present on create — true if calendar event was created.

appointment_updated.description: Present on update — true if calendar event was updated.

result.description:
Full CRM calendar API response. For create/update includes:
- `result` (1=success)
- `response_dict.id` — provider event ID
- `response_dict.htmlLink` — Google Calendar URL (if Google)
- `response_dict.webLink` — Outlook URL (if Microsoft)

NotificationInputSchema.description: Default input schema for notification nodes

NotificationNodeOutput.description:
Output from a notification node. Reflects the holistic endpoint response.
Use `channels` to check per-channel delivery status.

notification_sent.description: True if the holistic endpoint returned result=1.

notification_id.description: MongoDB IDs of the created in-app notification(s).

channels.description:
Per-channel delivery status from the holistic endpoint.
Values: 'sent', 'queued', 'skipped', 'skipped_no_valid_recipients',
'skipped_missing_fields', 'error'.

result.description: Full holistic endpoint response including result code and channel statuses.

DelayInputSchema.description: Input schema for delay nodes. Exactly one of `duration` or `target_timestamp` must be provided.

duration.description: Fixed delay duration (mutually exclusive with target_timestamp)

target_timestamp.description:
Template string resolving to Unix epoch seconds (mutually exclusive
with duration). Interpolated by the engine before evaluation.

offset_seconds.description:
Seconds to subtract from target_timestamp before computing delay.
**NOT interpolatable** — must be a literal int. Negative offsets
add (e.g. -5184000 → 60 days AFTER target).

jitter.description: Random jitter in seconds (literal int, not interpolatable).

ProspectActivityItem.description:
Single normalized item in the unified activity feed. The `channel`
field discriminates the source collection; `meta` carries
channel-specific extras (campaign_id, message_id, recording_url, etc.).

ts.description: Activity timestamp, epoch seconds. For email_logs, falls back to ObjectId generation_time when `created_ts` is absent.

direction.description:
Phone/email direction inferred from from/to vs. the prospect's
identity set. `null` for comments and when neither side matches.

body.description:
Message body / comment text / voicemail transcript. May be
truncated for campaign sends (first 500 chars).

matched_via.description:
Why this item joined the feed — e.g. `"phone"`, `"email"`,
`"lead.comments"`, `"contact.comments"`. Useful for debugging
when account fan-out joins many child contacts.

source_entity.description:
For comments, the entity whose inline `comments` array yielded
this item (relevant when account fan-out merges multiple
contacts). `null` for log-collection channels.

raw_id.description:
Underlying record id (ObjectId for log collections, UUID for
comments). Used as the secondary sort key and for boundary
dedupe across pages.

ProspectActivitiesResolvedRef.description:
Echoes the resolved entity (after lead→contact upgrade redirect),
the matched identity sets, and the original input when redirected.

redirected_from.description:
Present only when a converted lead was auto-redirected to its
contact. Carries the original `entity_type` / `entity_id` that
the caller passed in.

matched_emails.description: Normalized (lowercased) emails used in the email_logs query.

matched_phones.description: Phone variants (E.164 + 10-digit + 11-digit + raw) used in phone_log_events / voicemails queries.

ProspectActivitiesResponse.description:
Unified prospect activity feed response. `next_cursor` is `null` when
the page is not full (no further records). When non-null, the caller
should pass it as `before_ts` on the next request, AND dedupe items
whose `raw_id` is in `boundary_ids` to avoid double-counting at the
page boundary when multiple items share the cursor timestamp.

next_cursor.description:
Pass back as `before_ts` on the next request. `null` when the
current page is shorter than `page_size` (no more records).

boundary_ids.description:
`raw_id`s of items in the current page whose `ts` equals
`next_cursor`. Client should dedupe against these on the next
page to handle ts-collisions cleanly.

assignee.description: User ID to assign the lead to (alias for `userid`)

userid.description: User ID to assign the lead to (alias for `assignee`)

CalendarEventsJsonRequest.description:
JSON body for querying calendar events. Field names are mapped
from snake_case (workflow engine convention) to the camelCase
names the original calendar handler expects.

start_date.description: Start of date range (alias: start_date_time, startDateTime)

end_date.description: End of date range (alias: end_date_time, endDateTime)

event_id.description: Specific event ID to fetch (alias: eventId)

q.description: Free-text search query for event titles/descriptions

get_free_slots.description: When true, returns available time slots instead of events
